excluded: No builder notes, code, tests, other reviews, or comparison.mp4 inspected.

viewing_basis.limitation: Judgments concern the nine supplied source/key pairs and the source contact sheet. Continuous timing, transition smoothness, and absence of between-sample slipping are not verified.

overall: Close, but the source pose match needs one local repair before an unqualified pass.

source_pose_and_composition.assessment: Composition reads well: left helper and child, central fulcrum, crossing parallel equipment, and small background riders retain the source arrangement. The helper pose is the conspicuous mismatch: in the low phase, source-01 through source-03 and source-09 show a pronounced forward bend over the child/board, while the corresponding doodle remains an upright angular squat. The rise/return of the child is otherwise recognizably matched.

same_doodle_identity.assessment: The long outlined plank and simple triangular support remain identifiable as the supplied doodle, within a coherent sparse black-line scene. The more regular outline is acceptable; no visual restyling is needed.

hinge_action.assessment: Across the sampled keys the active plank rotates around the same central support, lifts the left rider to a high reversal around key-06/key-07, and returns to the initial low pose by key-09. This establishes the hinge mechanism in stills; it does not establish normal-speed motion quality.

rider_contact_and_occlusion.assessment: The child stays visibly coupled to the left end through the sampled cycle. The foreground diagonal equipment crosses in front and the active plank covers the fulcrum tip consistently enough to make the depth legible. Grounded helper feet are stable. Contact remains graphically simple, but no sampled frame shows a decisive detached rider or board-through-body failure.

one_gap_that_matters_most: The helper does not perform the source's deep forward bend during the low part of the cycle.
smallest_repair: Change only the helper's low-phase torso/head/arm articulation: hinge the torso forward over the left end and lower the head and reaching hand, blending into the existing upright high-phase pose. Keep the feet grounded, preserve child/board contact and foreground occlusion, and retain the current sparse doodle stroke style. Do not redraw the scene or add detail.
motion_approval: Not granted: actual normal-speed playback was not performed.
